title: Introduce traffic-adaptive probe sparsifier and fallback lattice for perf canaries
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Adds an adaptive probe sparsifier to reduce noisy probe traffic and a fallback lattice that progressively increases probe density when instability is detected. Includes rollout guard integration, dashboards, runbook updates, and automated rollback triggers.
description: Motivation: our continuous perf canaries occasionally trigger false-positive regressions during traffic spikes or when cohorts have high variance, which results in unnecessary rollbacks and alert noise. This change implements a traffic-adaptive probe sparsifier that dynamically reduces probe density when steady-state traffic and SLO headroom indicate low risk, and a fallback lattice that steps probe density back up deterministically when signals show degradation. Goals: lower probe-induced noise and cost, improve signal-to-noise ratio of canary evaluations, and provide deterministic fallback behavior so that regressions are still detected quickly. What changed: 1) core algorithm: a rolling-variance estimator + headroom calculator drives a sparsifier that throttles probe samples per tenant per-window; 2) fallback lattice: three discrete escalation tiers (sparse, normal, dense) with hysteresis and decay timers to avoid oscillation; 3) routing integration: probes can be shadowed to a replay queue for enrichment when an escalation is triggered; 4) rollout guard hooks: added thresholds (p50/p95/p99, error-rate delta, and throughput delta) with configurable time windows and confidence requirements; 5) ops: dashboards, runbook, and alert tuning; 6) tests: unit, deterministic sim harness, and integration runs in the perf-canary lab. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind ff/perf/sparsifier, staged rollout to 5% of tenants for 24h with synthetic probe burst tests, then 25% for 48h, then 100% if no regressions. Automated guard: if p95 latency increases > 20% with >95% confidence, or error-rate increases > 0.5pp and sustained for 3 windows, the rollout lattice forces immediate density increase and triggers an automatic rollback policy depending on severity. Backwards compatibility: algorithm runs as an opt-in config per canary and does not change historical metrics. Related work: follows ENG-3281 proposal for probe-cost-reduction and ENG-3302 for rollback lattice design. Checklist: - [x] design docs and linear tickets linked - [x] unit tests added - [x] simulation scenarios with synthetic traffic - [x] integration runs in perf-canary lab - [x] dashboards and runbook updated - [x] staged rollout plan and automated guard configured More context and the runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3281/perf-probe-sparsifier-runbook
